correctness.rationale: Separately affine tetrahedral determinants reduce the unrestricted maximum to vertex quadruples of the two-base convex polytope. The layer splitting is exhaustive: one-versus-three yields at most h(3sqrt(3)R^2/4)/3; two-versus-two gives h|det(u,v)|/6 for planar chord differences. The regular polygon difference body is regular n-gonal (n even) or 2n-gonal (n odd), with the stated circumradius and angular mesh. Bilinearity maximizes its determinant at difference-body vertices and yields the exact cosine-distance expression. Its worst twist still beats the three-on-one-layer bound strictly for n>=4 and matches only for the n=3 aligned exceptional class. The sharp angle endpoints follow from exact distance to the angular lattice. The standalone finite checker was executed with 110 exhaustive vertex-set samples and six numerical specializations; its finite scope is not used to prove the universal theorem.

originality.rationale: The investigated objective is an unrestricted tetrahedron maximum in the convex hull of two relatively rotated regular polygonal bases, for every n and all twists. Akopyan-Glazyrin's primary text gives qualitative prism-maximality structure, not this angular formula. The closest published regular-polygon results compute a single-body translative chord-width product or maximum area of a rectangle in an aligned even polygon; the latter can recover aligned benchmarks but neither implies the independently rotated two-body angular law. Genuine all-angle parity-dependent sharp bounds and reversal are the claimed contribution, with an acknowledged unindexed-priority risk.
residual_risks: An older unindexed recreational or specialized paper may state the same sharp twisted-prismatoid tetrahedron profile under different terminology.
The aligned even-n special cases are closely related to published optimal rectangle results; they are not individually credited as new.
This self-review is not independent mathematical or bibliographic certification.

value.rationale: The exact maximum inscribed tetrahedron volume is a natural geometric invariant of a well-motivated all-order one-parameter deformation linking regular prisms and antiprismatoids. Equation (1) resolves all continuous twist angles and integer orders, identifies all sharp minimizing and maximizing orientations and a reversal controlled by n modulo four. This supplies a precise benchmark for tetrahedral decomposition and a structural law not provided by known aligned-prism values; it is not a cosmetic renaming or isolated numerical evaluation.
